11. She has further pointed that both the Courts below has taken the erroneous view that if the Court execute the decree and dispossessed the defendants from the suit property they will not suffer in any injury and loss rather, opined that if the petitioner succeed in the Miscellaneous Case in that case the petitioner can recorded the possession of the suit property under section 144 of the Code. However, both the Courts below have forgotten if the pending Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code the ex-parte judgment and decree executed the Miscellaneous Case itself would be infructuous. Therefore, both the Courts below committed serious error of law hence, she prayed for make the Rule absolute setting aside the judgment and order of both the Courts below. 

 20. We are, therefore, of the considered view that the case of both the sides must be considered in juxta equilibration of the yardstick of justice although we find that the orders passed by the joint District Judge, Barguna and the learned District Judge as revisional Court never discussed any point in respect of the facts of the Miscellaneous Case rather, from their opinion it appears to us that they have taken the view that the ex-parte decree must be executed and the petitioner if succeed in the Miscellaneous Case in that case the petitioner would have a chance to recover the possession of the suit property under section 144 of the Code which adversely gone against the substantive justice. When both the parties under litigation to set-aside the ex-parte judgment and decree the executing Court must born in mind that if the petitioner has not given a chance to prove her allegation of fraud against the plaintiff in obtaining the ex-parte judgment and decree what would be consequence if after conclusion of the trial of Miscellaneous Case the petitioner is able to prove her allegation of fraud and why she would have to face another proceeding as opined by them.
